previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease, and gout was admitted with acute shortness of breath and chest pain. He had developed worsening dyspnea after his last dialysis session, associated with a recent upper respiratory infection. Imaging and labs revealed pulmonary edema and severe fluid overload, with a BNP over 70,000 and admission troponin elevation to 0.17, peaking at 0.38 without MB fraction rise or EKG changes. He was treated with nitroglycerin infusion and emergent hemodialysis, removing 3.2 liters initially and 2.4 liters on the second day. His symptoms improved, and he was weaned from BiPAP. The chest pain was atypical and not indicative of acute coronary syndrome. He was discharged home with instructions to continue dialysis, start benzonatate for cough, and adjust cinacalcet dose, with home health follow-up.

Brief Hospital Course:
# Reactive airways disease: Patient reports symptoms consistent 
with upper respiratory infection (low grade fever, cough, 
congestion) followed by dyspnea that improved with inhalers. He 
had a benign chest radiograph. Denies any history of asthma or 
other atopy but, nevertheless, symptoms seem very consistent 
with reactive airways disease. Symptoms improved with albuterol 
nebulizer treatments & mucinex.

# Cough/Low grade fever: Likely secondary to a viral upper 
respiratory infection. CXR had no evidence of infiltrate. 
Patient received guaifenesin with dextromethorphan for cough.

# Hyperkalemia: Likely secondary to ESRD; however, there was 
also concern about lisinopril in the context of his chronic 
kidney disease. Lisinopril was held, but restarted on discharge. 
Patient received HD.

# Chronic Diastolic CHF: Patient did not seem to be having an 
acute on chronic CHF exacerbation. Fluid was removed at dialysis 
and he remained euvolemic. Pt has normal EF on previous echo 
though does have LVH and HTN so high risk for diastolic CHF.

# End stage renal disease: Continued HD on normal schedule and 
home sevelamer.

# CAD: No signs or symptoms of ACS. Troponin less than baseline. 
Continued home beta-blocker, asprin, clopidogrel and 
pravastatin.

# DVT Prophylaxis: Patient received heparin products during this 
admission.

# Code status: Full code.

INDICATION:  The patient is a ___ male with shortness of breath
similar to previous.  Evaluate for effusion or edema.

EXAMINATION:  PA and lateral chest radiographs.

COMPARISONS:  Comparison is made to radiographs from ___ and
CT examinations from ___ and ___.

FINDINGS:  Since the most recent examination, previously noted interstitial
pulmonary edema has improved.  A known micronodular/interstitial pulmonary
abnormality is chronic, as better characterized on prior CT examinations. 
There are no new focal consolidations concerning for pneumonia. There are no
pleural effusions or pneumothorax.  The cardiomediastinal and hilar contours
are stable demonstrating moderate cardiomegaly and tortuosity of thoracic
aorta.  Pulmonary vascularity is normal.  Redemonstrated is sequelae of remote
trauma involving the left clavicle.  There are multilevel degenerative changes
of the thoracic spine and multiple wedge compression deformities.

IMPRESSION:

1.  No acute cardiopulmonary process.

2.  Known chronic interstitial/nodular abnormality as better characterized on
